leads.title: [agent] Any customer can modify shared product records via PUT /api/Products/:id (broken function-level authorization / integrity)

detail.text: Signed in as ordinary customer busl1 (user 31), PUT /api/Products/1 with body {"description":"integrity-test-busl-marker"} returned HTTP 200 and GET /api/Products/1 confirmed the description of the shared catalogue product was overwritten. No admin role is required, so any authenticated customer can tamper with product catalogue data (description, and by extension other writable fields). The test marker was restored to the original "The all-time classic." afterwards. A reviewer should confirm whether price/deluxePrice are likewise writable, which would allow direct price manipulation.

leads.title: [agent] Checkout can be completed with no address/payment and produces a negative order total

detail.text: As busl1 with no saved address (GET /api/Addresss = []) and wallet balance 0, POST /rest/basket/12/checkout with an empty body returned HTTP 200 and created order 215c-6334a78f722a6666. GET /rest/order-history shows the order with paymentId:null, addressId:null, and totalPrice -199 (product Apple Juice quantity -100, line total -199). Two business-logic defects combine: (1) the checkout workflow does not require address/payment selection server-side (steps enforced only in the UI), and (2) the negative basket-item quantity accepted earlier yields a negative order total. A reviewer should confirm whether a negative total credits the customer's wallet/account.

leads.title: [agent] Feedback can be posted in another user's name (client-controlled UserId)

detail.text: Signed in as busl1 (user 31), POST /api/Feedbacks with body {"UserId":1,"comment":"busl forged-userid test","rating":1,"captchaId":2,"captcha":"13"} returned 201. GET /api/Feedbacks shows the stored feedback id 10 with UserId:1 (the admin account). The endpoint trusts the client-supplied UserId instead of binding the feedback to the session, allowing feedback to be forged in any user's name.

leads.title: [agent] Feedback rating accepts out-of-range values (no min/max validation)

detail.text: POST /api/Feedbacks with {"comment":"...","rating":6,"captchaId":1,"captcha":"1"} returned 201 and GET /api/Feedbacks shows the stored record (id 9) with rating:6, even though the rating scale is 0-5. The rating field is not bounded server-side, allowing inflated/invalid ratings. The captcha gate is trivially solved because GET /rest/captcha returns the answer in cleartext.

leads.title: [agent] Negative basket-item quantity accepted (no data validation), enabling negative order totals

detail.text: As busl1 (user 31, own basket id 12, own basket item id 9), PUT /api/BasketItems/9 with {"quantity":-100} returned HTTP 200 and GET /rest/basket/12 confirms the item is persisted with quantity -100. By contrast the same endpoint enforces the per-user maximum (limitPerUser=5) for positive quantities (POST quantity 99 and PUT quantity 99 both returned 400). The quantity field is not validated for a positive/minimum value, so a negative quantity is stored and would yield a negative line total at checkout (classic Juice Shop negative-order business-logic flaw). Validation by a reviewer should confirm the resulting order/wallet effect.

leads.title: [agent] Privilege escalation: registration honours client-supplied role, creating an admin account

detail.text: Unauthenticated POST /api/Users with body {"email":"agent-busl-ma-7f3a@juice.lab.test","password":"[redacted:sha256:ab5df625bc76]","role":"admin"} returned HTTP 201. GET /api/Users/47 (the highest existing user id; 48+ return 404) shows the created account with role:"admin" and profileImage assets/public/images/uploads/defaultAdmin.png, createdAt 2026-10-16T20:32:03Z matching the request. The registration endpoint does not strip/ignore the role attribute (mass assignment), so any anonymous user can self-provision an administrator account — full privilege escalation. A reviewer may want to confirm admin capabilities by signing in to this account.

leads.title: [agent] Product review author is client-controlled (identity spoofing on PUT /rest/products/:id/reviews)

detail.text: Signed in as busl1 (email hash 787aacee7b7b per /rest/user/whoami), PUT /rest/products/2/reviews with body {"message":"busl-review-forge-test","author":"spoofed-victim@juice-sh.op"} returned 201. GET /rest/products/2/reviews shows the stored review with author set to the supplied value (hash 7117009045a3), not busl1's session email. The endpoint trusts the client-supplied author field instead of deriving it from the authenticated session, letting a user post reviews attributed to any arbitrary identity/email. (By contrast, POST /api/BasketItems targeting another user's BasketId=13 was correctly rejected with 401.)
